**The anti-pattern:** Devi Anand (Senior ML Engineer at DeepMind) says RAG is becoming an anti-pattern for most production LLM apps. Her post says agentic search with well-designed tool APIs beats traditional RAG pipelines:
- The retrieval step adds latency.
- Chunking introduces artifacts.
- Context windows are now big enough to skip retrieval for most use cases.

In her words: "The future is agents with access to structured APIs, not vector databases stuffed with PDFs." The post links to "Why Agentic Search Beats RAG" on deepmind.google. The feed shows the reactions as 2.2K rather than the exact 2156, but the post shows 347 comments.

**Top commenters:**
- Blair Morgan: "Great insights! Thanks for sharing." (12 likes)
- Imani Brooks: "Couldn't agree more. Well said!" (20 likes)
- Petra Johansson: "This resonates a lot. We faced the same challenges last quarter." (23 likes)

All the comments I saw were general praise and added nothing to the argument.

**What I did:**
- **Reaction:** The post shows "Insightful" as your reaction. On the way there, a mis-tap briefly set it to "Funny" before I corrected it.
- **TeamChat #product:** The summary is posted in the channel. Owen Price has already replied to it.
- **Note:** "Tech Reading Queue" is saved in Notes. It has the article title, the deepmind.google domain and 3 takeaways. The app only showed the domain, not the full article URL, so that is what the note contains.
